newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast products rebound despite futures.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast products rebound despite futures.

text.p: U.S. West Coast product prices gained strength late on Monday, rebounding from oversold conditions last week despite weak futures, traders said.
"It got pushed down too far (on Friday)," one dealer said, adding that refiners, beset by poor margins, increased buying at low ranges on Monday.

NYMEX unleaded gasoline futures for October delivery settled 1.02 cents lower at 60.07 cents a gallon. Bids for conventional regular gasoline in Los Angeles rose by one to 1.5 cents to 65.50/66.50 cents a gallon.
Discounts for San Francisco grade were two cents lower.
CARB gasoline in L.A. also bounced back one to 1.50 cents to 70.50/71.50 cents a gallon from Friday's selling pressure.
Bids for CARB diesel in L.A. firmed 0.5 cent to 74 cents while offers remained at 75 cents.
Jet fuel in L.A. rose a cent to 70.50/71.50, but were seen steady for the rest of the week, with supplies flush.
